{{Information
|Description=Thurber's Patent Printer, an early prototype typewriter invented and patented by Charles Thurber, Massachusetts, USA, in 1843 for use by the blind.  This is the drawing from US Patent No. 3228, dated August 26, 1843.  Two of his innovations that are still used in mechanical typewriters today are a cylinder to carry the paper in a moveable carriage that advances with each letter typed, and a mechanism to advance the paper by one line each time the carriage is returned.  Thurber never commercially developed this device, and by the 1900s the prototype was in a Worcester museum. For more information, see [http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/modelb/modelb_informal.html The typewriter: an informal history, 1977, IBM Archives], and [http://www.todayinsci.com/Events/Patent/Typewriter3228.htm Charles Thurber, US Patent No. 3228, Today in Science History]
